hedging.name: Dutch Bros

periods.commentary: Q3 2025: beverage, food and packaging 25.9% of company-operated shop revenue, +60bp y/y mainly from higher coffee; coffee expected to stay elevated into 2026.

periods.months_covered: ~3 months of green coffee inventory on hand (stated policy)
periods.commentary: 10-K: 'On average, we typically have approximately three months of green coffee bean inventory stored'; roasts in Grants Pass OR and Melissa TX; buys under fixed-price and price-to-be-fixed green coffee commitments (no amount given); no coffee derivatives (only an interest-rate swap).
Q1 2026 call: 'Coffee remains in the $2.80 to $3.00 range'; ~60bp total COGS pressure in FY26 guide; ~1.5pt price in Q1-Q2, ~1pt rolls off at start of Q3.
Q2 2026 call: higher coffee costs to keep weighing on H2; ~60bp FY COGS pressure incl. food program.

Q3 2026 call (4 Nov 2026): BF&P 25.6% of co-op shop revenue, guided ~27.5% for Q4; 'over 1 point of coffee pressure'; 'it takes 2 to 3 quarters for that to flow through our P&L'; ~$4m tariff refunds in Q3; may take more price.

hedging.notes: Dutch Bros does not quantify its green coffee purchase commitments in XBRL and uses no coffee derivatives; disclosure is qualitative (fixed-price and price-to-be-fixed physical contracts, ~3 months green inventory). Raw materials include green coffee, dairy and other inputs. Coffee cost lag of 2-3 quarters means 2026 C-price declines reach the P&L in 2027.

hedging.name: JDE Peet's

periods.commentary: FY23 base.
H1 2024: group price +2.4%; outlook cites 'continued inflation and volatility in green coffee prices' requiring more pricing in H2; APAC helped by lower-priced green coffee from inventories.
FY 2024: green coffee prices 'more than doubled, compared to a year ago', 'not expected to decline in the near term'; price +4.5%, vol/mix +0.7%; 2025 guide: organic adj. EBIT LSD decline.
H1 2025: green coffee on average >60% higher y/y; price +21.5% (Europe +15.4%, LARMEA +55.0%, Peet's +3.5%, APAC +7.7%); passing on 'only what is unavoidable'.

FY 2025: 'total cost inflation of EUR 1.6 billion' (green coffee plus other); price +19.5%, vol/mix -4.3%; inventories cash outflow EUR 349m (2024: 363m). Last standalone report before KDP took control on 1 Apr 2026.

hedging.notes: Releases give total inventories and commodity contract fair values only (small, Level 1); no notional, coverage months or hedge horizon. The 2024 annual report PDF could not be read here, so its financial-risk note was not checked. From Q2 2026 its numbers sit inside KDP.

hedging.name: Nestle

periods.commentary: FY 2025: pricing +2.8% with targeted increases in coffee and cocoa categories; gross margin -110bp on higher coffee and cocoa costs, tariffs and FX.

H1 2026: coffee OG 7.5% (RIG 2.9%, price 4.7%; Q2 price 3.6% and easing); coffee UTOP margin 19.0% (-100bp); gross margin -20bp to 46.4% on 'higher coffee and cocoa prices flowing through the P&L'; Nespresso margin -120bp on coffee inflation and tariffs; H2 to benefit from 'lower coffee and cocoa costs impacting the P&L'. Group derivative assets current CHF 690m (Dec 2025: 295m), not split by commodity.

hedging.notes: Group-level only; coffee is ~CHF 24bn of sales but inventory and hedges are not split by commodity. Note 12 (financial instruments, commodity hedge notional) of the 2025 statements could not be read (document text cut off), so no commodity notional is recorded. Q3 2026 sales update not checked.
